balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For SEEK Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For SEEK Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For SEEK Limited: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For SEEK Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For SEEK Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For SEEK Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For SEEK Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For SEEK Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

segmentRevenue.title: Segment revenue: ANZ vs Asia
segmentRevenue.content:
SEEK runs two job-ad marketplaces with different maturity and monetisation: ANZ (Australia and New Zealand, high yield per ad, low volume growth) and SEEK Asia / Jobstreet-JobsDB (Hong Kong, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand -- lower yield, the growth leg).

For SEEK Limited: ANZ still funds most of the group's earnings, but the long-run thesis depends on Asia's volume growth eventually translating into yield as those markets mature the way ANZ already has.

What to watch:

  • Asia revenue share of the group rising over time
  • ANZ growth slowing as the market saturates
  • FY2024 and earlier are blank -- the segment split was only broken out as a CSV column from FY2025

jobAdVolume.title: Job ad volume growth
jobAdVolume.content:
Job ad volume growth is the YoY change in the number of job ads placed -- the demand side of SEEK's marketplace (employers buying ads to reach candidates). ANZ is reported for the combined region and split by Australia and New Zealand; Asia is reported as paid ad volume only (SEEK Asia also carries free listings that are not disclosed here).

For SEEK Limited: ANZ volume has been negative or flat in a soft hiring market (Australia -2% to -14% across recent periods) while SEEK is pushing Asia's paid volume as the growth lever -- so a negative Asia print (FY2026: -12%) is a bigger concern for the thesis than a negative ANZ print.

What to watch:

  • Australia vs New Zealand divergence within ANZ
  • Whether Asia paid volume reaccelerates after a soft period
  • Volume growth versus yield growth -- SEEK has offset weak ANZ volume with price (yield) increases

jobAdYield.title: Job ad yield (price) growth
jobAdYield.content:
Yield is revenue per job ad -- effectively SEEK's pricing power. Yield growth is the YoY change in that average price, reported for ANZ and for SEEK Asia's paid ads.

For SEEK Limited: yield growth has consistently outpaced volume growth in both segments (ANZ yield +10% to +17% against volume declines; Asia paid yield +17% to +20%), which is how revenue has kept growing through a volume downturn -- but price increases cannot offset shrinking volume indefinitely.

What to watch:

  • Yield growth decelerating once price increases meet customer resistance
  • Revenue growth (chart above) reconciling to roughly volume growth + yield growth for each segment

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For SEEK Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For SEEK Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
